description: Machine-readable definition of the dcc-mcp Python adapter contract: the interface rules that keep 50 adapter packages from re-inventing the same Core API, and the code-convention rules that keep their pyproject.toml files comparable. Consumed by scripts/check_repo_contract.py --contract and by the nightly sweep in .github/workflows/adapter-contract-nightly.yml. Rule ids use the A0xx namespace so that a repository can run this contract alongside contract/repo_contract.json (R0xx) without ambiguity.

profiles.baseline: Rules every Python adapter package satisfies today. Two interface rules that are mechanically decidable and safe to enforce immediately (no Core floor bump needed).
profiles.strict: Adds the convergence rules. Everything here is a warning on purpose: this profile is the stock-take list for PIP-4101, not a same-day blocker. Promote a rule with --error-rule once its owning repository is clean.

rules.name: no-deprecated-install-sop-alias
rules.title: Adapter code never references Core's deprecated Install SOP alias
rules.summary: Core 0.20.40 renamed INSTALL_SOP_SCHEMA_VERSION to INSTALL_SOP_SCHEMA_REVISION and serves the old name through a __getattr__ that raises DeprecationWarning. The old name is the schema *artifact* revision, not the report field: copying it into a report's schema_version is the defect PIP-4047/4048/4049/4050/4051 fixed one repository at a time. Removing the reference needs no Core floor bump, because every existing reference already sits behind a try/except ImportError fallback.

rules.name: no-hand-rolled-report-schema-version
rules.title: The report schema version is read from Core, not re-declared locally
rules.summary: A module-level `*_REPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION = <int>` is a hand-written copy of what install_sop_report_schema_version() now returns by reading the schema `const`. Every copy is a second source of truth that drifts the day Core republishes the artifact. Warns only: converging these needs the Core floor raised to >=0.20.40 first, which PIP-4101 owns.

rules.name: core-floor-declared
rules.title: A declared dcc-mcp-core dependency pins an explicit lower bound
rules.summary: Reads [project.dependencies] and [tool.poetry.dependencies] only. An unversioned `dcc-mcp-core` resolves to whatever happens to be installed, which is how the 54-patch floor spread (>=0.18.2 .. >=0.20.36) appeared. A repository that declares no Core dependency at all is out of scope and is skipped rather than failed.

rules.name: ruff-line-length
rules.title: [tool.ruff] line-length is the organisation baseline
rules.summary: Three values (100 / 110 / 120) coexist across the fleet. 120 is the baseline because core, maya, blender, houdini, nuke, zbrush, substance3d-* and touchdesigner already use it, so converging on 120 is the smallest diff. A repository with no [tool.ruff] line-length at all is reported as undeclared rather than as wrong, because the two need different fixes.

rules.name: requires-python-declared
rules.title: project.requires-python is declared
rules.summary: An undeclared requires-python lets pip install the package on any interpreter the wheel happens to accept. This rule deliberately does NOT pick a value: host-side constraints are legitimate (zbrush, wwise and obs need >=3.10), and the organisation Python 3.7 red line (PIP-2519) runs to 2026-12-31. Visibility only.

rules.name: pre-commit-config-exists
rules.title: .pre-commit-config.yaml exists at the repository root
rules.summary: Without it, the ruff settings in pyproject.toml only run in CI, so a contributor learns about a lint failure after pushing. 6 of 50 packages have one today.

rules.name: doctor-module-present
rules.title: An adapter that provides install capability ships a doctor self-check module
rules.summary: The doctor is where an adapter assembles its Install SOP report and validates it before the report is published. 8 of 50 adapters have one (openusd, material-maker, wwise, freecad, sketchup, openscad, liquigen, capcut), so the rule is a convergence warning and the gap closes by ratchet. Adapters with no install surface are skipped rather than reported. Ids A007-A012 are unassigned: this family was numbered A010-A014 by PIP-4106 before A001-A006 existed, and its first three rules were superseded by A001, A002 and A003 rather than renumbered.
known_boundaries: The module is matched by name, so a doctor that assembles a report without validating it satisfies the rule.
install_source_globs matches src/**/install*.py, so install_preflight_docs.py counts as install capability while uninstall.py does not.
rules.remediation: Add a doctor module that assembles the Install SOP report and validates it with validate_install_sop_report().

rules.name: report-validates-against-schema
rules.title: A real report is validated with validate_install_sop_report() in tests or CI
rules.summary: An adapter that assembles an Install SOP report has to validate a real report against the schema at least once, in a test or in a CI workflow: those are the only places that run before the artefact is published. Every adapter in the PIP-3990 incident shipped a schema and none of them ran a report through it, which is how the wrong value reached a release.
known_boundaries: The validator is matched as text over the scan globs, so a mention in a comment or in a TODO line satisfies the rule.
rules.remediation: Call validate_install_sop_report() on the report a doctor run actually produces, not on a hand-written fixture.

deprecated_symbols.INSTALL_SOP_SCHEMA_VERSION: Core 0.20.40 renamed it to INSTALL_SOP_SCHEMA_REVISION. The old name is the schema *artifact* revision, not the report's schema_version field: where the value genuinely means the artifact revision, rename it; where it feeds a report's schema_version or is a vestigial import, delete the reference and read the field from install_sop_report_schema_version() instead.
